summary: The algebraic elimination from the relaxed inequalities is coherent, but the candidate incorrectly identifies (5) as the exact two-cap condition for the stated support hexagon. The common inner support parameter is geometrically tied to the southwest edge and cannot be chosen independently of a and b.
critical_errors: In the nondegenerate case a,b>0, the common inner support line through (a,0) and (0,b) has equation y+tau*x=b=tau*a, so its slope parameter necessarily satisfies tau=b/a. Equation (5) instead existentially quantifies tau independently of a and b. It therefore admits tuples that cannot have the asserted common inner support line and is only a relaxation, contrary to the statement that it is the exact two-cap constraint. The cases with a=0 or b=0 also require separate incidence analysis; a finite common line through two distinct axis points cannot exist when exactly one of them is zero.
gaps: The cap-triangle argument proves only that an actual geometric completion yields the two inequalities in (5). It gives no converse realization showing that every tuple satisfying (5), with the stated southwest edge and exact cap areas, comes from the claimed support-hexagon geometry.
repair_hints: Include the missing incidence relation between tau and the southwest edge, with a separate treatment of the coincident-origin case, and prove any claimed converse realization. Otherwise describe (5) explicitly as a necessary relaxation rather than an exact geometric characterization.
